required_corrections: APPROVE with two required corrections. (1) when_not_to_use is under-specified: it bars repeating the invitation only after the concern is already clear, so it does not catch back-to-back duplicate invitations while the concern is still vague. Example 4 (9f34c2d1) is exactly that case - the supporter asks can you explain further and then Can you tell me more? with no intervening seeker turn - which is the repeated_question risk the card already claims to carry. Amend to: do not issue a second open invitation before the user has had a turn to respond, regardless of whether the concern is clear. (2) Replace example 4 with a clean instance; with the amended wording it becomes a negative example. Examples 2 and 5 are near-identical (How can I help you? / Hey! How can I help?) and example 3 is a third variant of the same formula, so 3 of 5 fixed sources instantiate one surface form; add at least one mid-dialogue invitation to cover the exploration phase the card claims. Example 3 also has the supporter answering after four unanswered seeker turns without acknowledging the wait - not a hard exclusion, but a poor exemplar of warmth.

DO NOT ADVANCE UNTIL SOURCE EXAMPLES ARE RE-DRAWN. The card text and the 45-dialogue gate are sound; the fixed source set is not. Example 2 (7dba4790) stacks two questions and prefixes them with a motive attribution (your co-worker doesn't trust your abilities), violating the card's own do-not-stack rule plus AM04's unsupported-inference bar. Example 4 (8a12fcc4) is not a clarification at all - it is a directive workplace suggestion that belongs to AM10 - and it is the SAME blind_item_id used as example 4 of AM05, so one response is being used as evidence for two different moves and the manifest's fixed_source_example_count of 40 is really 39 unique items. Example 5 (b6f8a26c) asks What exactly is the problem?, which is an open re-invitation (AM01) rather than one focused clarification, and it re-opens ground already covered earlier in the same window. Required: drop examples 2, 4 and 5, redraw three single-question instances, and add a global de-duplication check across all eight cards before re-review.

DO NOT ADVANCE UNTIL EXAMPLE 5 IS REMOVED AND A HIGH-STAKES CARVE-OUT IS ADDED. Example 5 (c693cbe1) is the most serious problem in the whole packet: the visible window contains I feel like dying all the time, and the target response paraphrases the shame content while leaving that line entirely unaddressed. The line is also attributed to the SUPPORTER, which looks like a turn-segmentation error in the source; either way this item must not sit in a fixed bank as a positive exemplar. It also exposes a structural gap: only AM14 and AM15 carry any high-stakes clause, so AM01, AM02, AM04, AM05, AM07 and AM10 would all license their move on top of an unhandled risk cue. Add a bank-wide hard exclusion (do not apply this move in place of responding to an active self-harm, violence or crisis cue) and re-audit every fixed example for such cues. Example 2 (f7136172) hardens the user's account into a causal claim (the pandemic has CAUSED your fear) and drops the shame theme the user actually foregrounded (going home as a loser), which is the stronger-conclusion exclusion; replace it. Example 3 (2e072669) renders one night we hooked up as a one-time encounter, a mild frequency hardening - defensible inside the visible window, flagged as uncertain. Example 5's compound form (paraphrase plus an added question) should also be noted: the card is defined as a pure restate-and-check with directive_burden none, so compound instances should be excluded or the card should say the check may carry one follow-up.

Best-written card in the packet - the exclusion list (invent or intensify emotion, diagnose, minimize, promise an outcome, validate a harmful claim) is the model the other cards should follow. But 3 of 5 fixed sources violate it, so DO NOT ADVANCE UNTIL RE-DRAWN. Example 1 (1a61b1c3): the validation is a single clause and the turn's real content is a leading counter-question (Would your siblings not be able to...) that pushes back on the concern the user just stated - that is the minimize exclusion. Example 2 (f7049098): There is no need to feel embarrassed overrides a feeling the user explicitly reported; telling a user not to feel something is the inverse of grounded validation and is already barred as minimizing. Example 4 (8a12fcc4): DUPLICATE of AM02 example 4; the four-word validation (that is frustrating) is a preface to a directive suggestion, so as an AM05 exemplar it teaches the model to fuse validation with advice - exactly the conflation the mode/phase/burden metadata is designed to prevent (AM05 is directive_burden none). Also note example 2 and AM07 example 3 both come from esconv_0793, and AM07's target response appears verbatim inside example 2's visible context, so the two cards' evidence is not independent. Required: replace examples 1, 2, 4; enforce one dialogue per card per source and no shared dialogues across cards.

REJECT THE NARROW EXCEPTION. The card definition itself is fine, but the exception must be judged on whether the fixed sources justify going below the 20-dialogue gate, and they do the opposite. Four of five violate the card's own hard exclusions, and the violations are of its single most important one, generic praise. Example 4 (a4750f7b) is literally Good effort, keep it up! and example 5 (d95bb58e) is Nice! Good job with those things. immediately after the user named three specific efforts the response declines to name - both are pure generic praise, i.e. negative examples sitting in a positive bank. Example 3 (d03335c4) ends with I think you can get through this, which is the barred outcome promise (false_reassurance). Example 1 (50a8887b) infers an unshown trait (a strong family) from the user's own much weaker report that they have helped SOME, and redirects away from the meaninglessness the user had just stated. Example 2 (2565e93f) anchors on a near-degenerate effort (typing) and opens with The only thing that matters is, which minimizes the user's concern. With 17 clean dialogues, a 0.4211 single-problem share, and a 4/5 exclusion-violation rate in the hand-picked evidence, the weak-source extraction for this move is not reliable enough to ship. Per post_review_rule this card is not to be replaced by new weak-source expansion; if the acknowledge-effort function is considered essential, it should be rebuilt from a fresh source pass with generic praise filtered at extraction time, not readmitted through the exception route.

DO NOT ADVANCE. The card is well specified (one step, low risk, low burden, easy to decline) and this is the highest-burden move in the bank, so evidence quality matters most here. Only example 2 (6d411af2) is a clean instance - one concrete step plus an explicit Would you consider trying this. Example 1 (fcc33d10) offers no step at all, just a general principle about small adjustments, so there is nothing to decline. Example 3 (1c2b638f) repeats advice already given twice in the same window after the user had already agreed, and states it as I suggest you try to talk to her today - prescriptive with a deadline, i.e. excessive_directiveness. Example 4 (283e7f5e) stacks two tasks (bath AND cocoa), is not declinable, and lands on a user who has just said they have been crying for hours - an acute-distress moment where an action step is the wrong phase; its visible context also contains a legal claim about organisations that will help you get the dog back (domain_claim) and the supporter steering the breakup, so the surrounding turn quality is poor. Example 5 (0cb65bb6) is properly hedged but the step is not tied to the goal under discussion (the user was working on the job item; the supporter suggests an exercise class) and a paid class sits awkwardly against a stated financial constraint. SEPARATE STRUCTURAL ISSUE: when_to_use requires that advice help be EXPLICITLY welcomed, and none of the five source examples shows an explicit invitation. If the extractor cannot enforce that precondition, G2 will learn the step without the permission gate that makes it safe. Either add explicit-invitation evidence to every fixed example or move the permission check into the card as a required precondition the generator must satisfy at run time.

APPROVE with corrections. This is the only card that already names unhandled_high_stakes_cue and availability_overclaim, and its exclusion list is the one that should be propagated to the rest of the bank. Required: (1) Remove example 1 (1e982abb). It violates the card's own ignore-an-active-high-stakes-cue exclusion - the user says I can't accept this pain and then asks to end the session, the preceding supporter turn is false reassurance (things will be better with time), and the target turn re-opens the conversation the user had just asked to close. It is a negative example for both the high-stakes and the respect_boundary branches. (2) Fix the exemplar diversity: examples 3, 4 and 5 are the same closing formula (Can I help with anything else / Anything else I can help you with today), so 3 of 5 sources cover one surface form and the change-focus branch named in the support_move has no exemplar at all. Add at least one mid-dialogue topic-shift offer and one instance where the user signals fatigue rather than completion. (3) Example 4 (6b0c88f4) is marked uncertain: the supporter themself raised a possible partner-aggression risk (may get jealous and aggressive) two turns earlier and then moves to close without returning to it; the transition is well formed but the thread is left open. (4) 21 clean dialogues is a thin pass on a 20 gate - if any example is removed without replacement, re-check that the gate still holds.

REJECT THE NARROW EXCEPTION. This is the worst risk-to-evidence ratio in the packet: the move that can most easily shape an irreversible relationship decision has the weakest base - 11 clean dialogues against a gate of 20, only 4 problem types, and 0.5455 of them from a single problem type, so over half the evidence is one scenario. The card text is also internally inconsistent: risk_flags declares values_imposition but when_not_to_use never excludes it, and example 3 (0c483520) shows why that matters - Do you feel that a little time would help you accept his apology and forgive him presupposes forgiveness and reconciliation as the endpoint. directive_burden light also looks understated for a move whose outputs in this very sample include telling users to keep distance from a friend or stop speaking to someone. On the examples: example 5 (d28c8e14) is I definitely suggest you keep some distance from her, which prescribes separation, the card's explicit bar, and its context (a friend's act the user's partner does not know about, shared workplace) is precisely the kind of loaded situation the card says to stay out of. Example 4 (f90f0fb7) infers the third party's motives (sometimes they just need their space), also explicitly barred, and walks back advice the user had directly asked to confirm. Example 1 (f3be6c19) endorses boundaries in the abstract rather than helping consider a specific one. Example 2 (467005c0) is the only reasonable instance and it still edges toward endorsing never speaking to the third party again. Example 3's user also has very limited English (He say that lie i will hurt), so comprehension of a nuanced boundary prompt cannot be assumed - a general caution for the source pool. Additionally, the abuse carve-out in when_not_to_use has no screening step attached, so as written the card licenses ordinary boundary guidance whenever abuse has not been explicitly disclosed. Rejecting leaves the bank with no boundary card, which on this evidence is the safer outcome; if the function is required it should be rebuilt from a dedicated source pass with a mandatory high-stakes screen, not admitted through the exception route.
